entries.title: ECDC Data, Dashboards and Databases (infectious disease surveillance)
entries.description: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control's hub for EU/EEA infectious-disease surveillance data: the Surveillance Atlas of Infectious Diseases, the European Respiratory Virus Surveillance Summary (ERVISS), antimicrobial consumption (ESAC-Net), vaccination coverage and polio dashboards, downloadable datasets and maps.
entries.publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: the newest existing capture (Save Page Now returned 0).

coverage.spatial: EU/EEA member states (some datasets global, e.g. MERS-CoV maps)

entries.license: ECDC intellectual property notice (ECDC-owned material CC-BY-4.0; third-party surveillance data reusable for commercial and non-commercial purposes with the prescribed source acknowledgement)
entries.attribution: Dataset provided by ECDC based on data provided by public health authorities, scientific institutes or health care providers in the relevant reporting countries and/or by WHO.
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The issue's URL https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/data redirects to https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/data-dashboards-and-databases, which is catalogued here. The page says "All data on topics in the area of infectious diseases collected by ECDC are made accessible in various formats, such as interactive databases and dashboards, downloadable datasets and maps." It links ERVISS, the Surveillance Atlas of Infectious Diseases, EpiPulse, the ESAC-Net antimicrobial consumption dashboard, the ECDC Geoportal, RespiCast, the vaccination coverage dashboard, the Vaccine Scheduler and the polio dashboard. The latest map listed is "Polio dashboard", 16 October 2026. It also links an "EU/EEA surveillance open data policy". The individual tools' download formats and APIs weren't checked, so format is left empty. Cadence varies by tool (ERVISS is weekly), so it is recorded as irregular. EpiPulse is ECDC's surveillance portal and was not checked for login requirements.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: ECDC's intellectual property notices (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ecdc-intellectual-property-notices) say "Unless otherwise stated, information and documents made publicly available on ECDC web pages and for which ECDC owns the copyright are licenced in accordance with the CC BY 4.0 licence". Under "Third party data in ECDC databases", the data "have been provided to ECDC by the public health authorities ... and/or by WHO. Except where otherwise stated, these data may be downloaded and reproduced for commercial and non-commercial purposes as long as the source of these data is acknowledged" in the form given in attribution, and modifications must be stated.

entries.title: Eurostat Health Statistics Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU health statistics: health status and healthy life years, health determinants (European Health Interview Survey), health care resources, expenditure and activities, causes of death, and health and safety at work, harmonised across EU member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: Eurostat free re-use policy (data reuse authorised for commercial or non-commercial purposes provided the source is acknowledged; Commission Decision of 12 December 2011)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The page is "Database - Health - Eurostat", with "Selected datasets" and "Detailed datasets" tabs whose dataset tree loads by JavaScript and did not render in the headless session. Eurostat's catalogue table of contents (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/catalogue/toc/txt?lang=en) answered HTTP 200 and lists a "Health" folder (code hlth) with subfolders "Health status", "Health determinants", "Health care", "Causes of death" and "Health and safety at work", holding 496 datasets. The latest data update listed is 27.10.2026, and "Causes of death - deaths by country of residence and occurrence" (hlth_cd_aro) was last updated 23.09.2026. A JSON request for hlth_cd_aro through the dissemination API (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/) returned HTTP 200. The formats listed are Eurostat's usual download options and weren't checked one by one.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: Eurostat's "Copyright notice and free re-use of data" (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says editorial content "is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence", and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged. The reuse policy of the European Commission is implemented by the Decision of 12 December 2011." Exceptions cover third-party material and data "identified as belonging to sources other than Eurostat" (non-commercial reuse only). The notice ties CC BY 4.0 to editorial content, and the data sentence names no licence, so this entry quotes the data reuse terms rather than labelling them CC-BY-4.0, as some sibling Eurostat entries do.

entries.title: openFDA
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's open API and bulk downloads over its public data: drug, device, food, animal and tobacco adverse-event reports (including FAERS), recall enforcement reports, drug labels, the NDC directory, Drugs@FDA, device 510(k)/PMA/UDI data and more.

access.auth_note: Free API key recommended; without one, limits are lower (see rate_limit)
access.rate_limit: No key: 240 requests/minute and 1,000/day per IP; with a free key: 240/minute and 120,000/day per key

coverage.spatial: United States (FDA-regulated products; adverse-event reports can originate abroad)

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (openFDA Terms of Service, "unless otherwise noted"; some third-party works are marked as not public domain)
entries.attribution: Data provided by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (https://open.fda.gov)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The home page offers "Open-source APIs" and "Download openFDA Data ... in zipped JSON format". The downloads page (https://open.fda.gov/data/downloads/) lists endpoints from Animal & Veterinary to Tobacco; for example "Drug Adverse Events [/drug/event] ... There are 1767 files, last updated on 2026-10-29" and Drug Labeling "last updated on 2026-10-30". It notes that animal and veterinary adverse events are updated quarterly, so cadence varies by endpoint; "weekly" is an approximation from the update dates seen, not a documented schedule. A key-less call to https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?limit=1 returned JSON. The authentication page says "An API key is required to make calls to the openFDA API. The key is free of charge", yet it also lists limits "With no API key: 240 requests per minute, per IP address. 1,000 requests per day, per IP address", so auth_required is false here.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: openFDA Terms of Service (https://open.fda.gov/terms/), "Data Rights and Usage": "Unless otherwise noted, the content, data, documentation, code, and related materials on openFDA is public domain and made available with a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication." It adds: "Some data on openFDA may not be public domain, such as copies of copyrightable works made available to the FDA by private entities", and such works are marked with a warning. Attribution is "not required" but requested in the form given above.

entries.title: ClinicalTrials.gov
entries.description: The U.S. National Library of Medicine's registry and results database of clinical studies conducted in the United States and around the world, with a public REST API and bulk download of study records.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine, National Institutes of Health (NIH)

coverage.spatial: global (studies in the United States and many other countries)

entries.license: ClinicalTrials.gov Terms and Conditions (free to all requesters, attribution required; not public domain outside the US)
entries.attribution: ClinicalTrials.gov (with the date the data were processed by ClinicalTrials.gov)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The site links the "ClinicalTrials.gov API" (https://clinicaltrials.gov/data-api/api), "How to Download Study Records" and FHIR access; the About API page lists CSV and RIS downloads and a JSON study data structure. The v2 API answered: /api/v2/version returned apiVersion 2.0.5 with dataTimestamp 2026-10-30T09:00:04, and /api/v2/stats/size reported totalStudies 609551.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the Terms and Conditions (https://clinicaltrials.gov/about-site/terms-conditions, last updated January 31, 2023) say "ClinicalTrials.gov data are available to all requesters, both within and outside the United States, at no charge." Users "should: Attribute the source of the data as ClinicalTrials.gov", keep the data current, "Clearly display the date the data were processed by ClinicalTrials.gov" and state any modifications. They also say "The ClinicalTrials.gov data carry an international copyright outside the United States" and "Some ClinicalTrials.gov data may be subject to the copyright of third parties". So it is not catalogued as plain public domain. Rate limits and the bulk-download formats beyond CSV/JSON weren't checked.

entries.title: OECD Health Statistics
entries.description: The OECD's cross-country database on health spending and health systems: health expenditure and financing (System of Health Accounts), health status, risk factors, healthcare human and provider resources, healthcare use, quality and outcomes, pharmaceutical markets, coverage and long-term care, for OECD members and selected partner countries.
entries.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

coverage.spatial: OECD member countries and selected partner economies

entries.license: OECD Terms and Conditions, Data section (any purpose including commercial, with credit to the OECD; third-party restrictions may apply)
entries.attribution: OECD, OECD Health Statistics (OECD Data Explorer)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl; the Data Explorer is a JavaScript app and was read in headless Chromium). The issue's URL, https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/oecd-health-statistics.html, returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to curl, headless Chromium (new headless mode, 25-second wait) and WebFetch, so this entry points at the OECD Data Explorer, where OECD serves the data. With the Topic facet set to Health it reports "86 datasets found", grouped into "Health expenditure and financing" (5), "Health status" (16), "Risk factors for health" (7), "Healthcare human resources" (16), "Healthcare provider resources" (6), "Healthcare use" (10), "Healthcare quality and outcomes" (14), "Pharmaceutical market" (4), "Healthcare coverage" (1) and "Long-term care" (4). The SDMX API (https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/) answered HTTP 200 and lists these under agency OECD.ELS.HD, for example DSD_SHA@DF_SHA "Health expenditure and financing" and DSD_HEALTH_STAT@DF_LE "Life expectancy". I did not confirm that every OECD.ELS.HD dataflow belongs to the product OECD brands "OECD Health Statistics", and I did not see a latest release date. The formats are taken from the Data Explorer's usual download and API options and weren't tested.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The Data Explorer's terms link goes to https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, which was blocked as above. Another vertical's entry (labor-almanac oecd-employment-labour-market) quotes those terms as allowing reuse of Data "for any purpose, even for commercial use" with credit. I could not read them this session, so no licence is asserted here.
Licence re-checked 2026-11-01: OECD Terms & Conditions (https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, read in headless Chromium; earlier attempts met a Cloudflare check), section 3 "Data": "you can extract from, download, copy, adapt, print, distribute, share and embed Data for any purpose, even for commercial use", with credit to the OECD using the dataset's citation. The section also says Data "may be subject to restrictions beyond the scope of these Terms and Conditions" where third parties own them; per-indicator source notes were not checked. These are OECD's own terms, not a named open licence.

entries.title: SAMHSA National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH)
entries.description: The main U.S. federal survey of tobacco, alcohol and drug use, substance use disorders, mental health and treatment among the civilian noninstitutionalized population aged 12 and older, with national, state and substate reports, detailed tables and public-use microdata files.
entries.publisher: U.S. Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality

access.auth_note: Public-use files download freely; restricted-use files require an application to a Research Data Center

coverage.spatial: United States (national, state and substate estimates; public-use files exclude most geography)

entries.license: SAMHSA data Terms of Use (use solely for research or statistical purposes; no re-identification of respondents)
entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality. (year). National Survey on Drug Use and Health (year). Retrieved from https://www.samhsa.gov/data/
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). On the page, releases read as follows: the headline is "SAMHSA Releases Results from the 2025 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH)". It says "This release includes a user-friendly infographic report, a more comprehensive report, detailed tables, and an accompanying methodology report", and the year selector for national reports runs from 2025 back to "1998-2014". The most recent spotlights listed are dated 9/30/2026 and 8/31/2026, and the page shows "Last Updated: 9/30/2026". The Download Data Files page (…/nsduh-national-survey-drug-use-and-health/datafiles, "Last Updated: 2/13/2025") lists public-use files from NHSDA 1979 to "NSDUH 2024" and "NSDUH 2021-2024"; no 2025 public-use file was listed there. Downloads are offered in SAS, SPSS, Stata, ASCII, delimited and R, with PDF codebooks and xlsx crosswalks. The page says "PUFs will generate comparable, but not identical, estimates to those published by SAMHSA because of the PUFs disclosure-avoidance methods." It also notes that 2021-onward data "cannot be compared or pooled with earlier years". Restricted-use files are available through NCHS Research Data Centers. I did not open or test the individual download files.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: SAMHSA's data Terms and Conditions (https://www.samhsa.gov/data/about-us/terms-and-conditions) say "By using SAMHSA's data, you agree to the Terms of Use listed on this page". Users of data agree "To use these datasets solely for research or statistical purposes", that "They cannot use it for re-identification of specific research subjects", and "To make no use of the identity of any research subject discovered inadvertently". Although it is a federal agency's product, these use conditions apply, so the entry is not marked plain public domain. The citation format comes from SAMHSA's FAQ "Why and how should I cite SAMHSA data?".

entries.title: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO)
entries.description: The World Health Organization's portal for global health statistics — curated indicators on mortality, disease burden, health systems, and the determinants of health for WHO member states.
entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 with WHO additional terms (WHO data terms and conditions, data.who.int)
entries.attribution: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory
entries.notes:
Programmatic access via the GHO OData API (https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: WHO's data terms (https://data.who.int/about/data/terms-and-conditions, repeated on data.who.int indicator pages) say "Unless specifically indicated otherwise, these Datasets are provided to you under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), with the additional terms below" (attribution, no de-anonymisation or misrepresentation, arbitration, termination). The CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licence recorded here earlier is WHO's licence for publications. The GHO pages themselves state no licence, and an older WHO data policy page (https://www.who.int/about/policies/publishing/data-policy/terms-and-conditions) still grants use only "for public health purposes"; that the GHO falls under the data.who.int terms is an inference a steward may want to confirm.

entries.title: WHO Mortality Database
entries.description: Global mortality data reported annually by WHO Member States from civil registration and vital statistics systems, with cause-of-death detail for comparative epidemiological studies.
entries.attribution: World Health Organization, WHO Mortality Database
entries.notes:
The WHO page states that the database is compiled from mortality data reported annually by Member States and that the visualization/export portal covers cause-of-death data from 1950 to date. The raw data section was last updated on 23 February 2026 when verified on 2026-08-03.
WHO states that no commercial use permission is implied for these transmitted data, and the database page does not identify a named license, so the license field is intentionally narrower than the WHO GHO catalog entry.
